item.title: North Carolina’s opaque national forests are about to get even more secretive
item.description: Last month, James Melonas, the supervisor of North Carolina’s national forests, signed off on a Helene recovery plan that could span tens of thousands of acres of the Pisgah National Forest over several years. While the Post Helene Reforestation and Revegetation Plan includes many obviously beneficial measures, close observers said, its vagueness and unusually broad scope could allow for disruptive activities, such as logging and roadbuilding, in vulnerable and ecologically valuable areas

item.description: In 2025, Buncombe County saw hotel occupancy rise and vacation rentals decline slightly, driven by reduced rental inventory and lingering post-Tropical Storm Helene demand.

item.title: The hellbender was slated for federal protection. It’s still in limbo
item.description: Because they breathe through their skin, the critters require pristine water. But after spending 160 million years living quietly in the same waters their ancient ancestors did, pollution, habitat loss and collection for the illegal pet trade have driven them ever closer to the graveyard of geologic history.
